title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's 'variations on the loop equation' (équation des lacets). Here he tests a matrix model in GL2 over a commutative ring or field. All brackets are group commutators, [x,y] = x y x^{-1} y^{-1}.

The parameters rho and sigma are companion-type matrices. In the notation of (51), rho = (0 v1; v w) and sigma = (0 v1'; v' w'). On the previous page he had the normalised case v1 = 1, v1' = -1, v' = -v, w' = 1 - w. So rho and sigma have the same determinant -v v1 and traces adding up to v1.

Previous page: he took alpha = u, an upper-triangular Borel element (mu lambda; 0 1). He computed xi = [u, rho] and eta = [u, sigma] explicitly (formula (46)). He observed that the right-hand column of xi (B = lambda/mu, D = 1/mu) recovers u: mu = 1/D, lambda = B/D (formulas (47), (48)).

This page, first part: the same holds for eta = (R S; T U). Its right column equals that of xi: S = B = lambda/mu and U = D = 1/mu. Hence u = (1/U S/U; 0 1) (formulas (47 bis), (48 bis)). This is consistent with (46), where the second columns of xi and eta coincide.

This page, second part: he moves to the general equation (49), [alpha, rho] = [beta, sigma] eps1(mu^{-1}). Here alpha and beta are arbitrary matrices, alpha = (a b; c d) and beta = (r s; t u). eps1(mu^{-1}) is presumably a diagonal or Borel correction factor. He renames u to v1 to avoid clashing with the entry u of beta, and imposes the constraints (52). He then writes out xi = [alpha, rho] using:
- alpha rho = (bv, a v1 + b w; dv, c v1 + d w);
- alpha^{-1} rho^{-1} = (1/(delta_alpha (-v v1))) (dw + bv, -d v1; -cw - av, c v1).

He gets the 'simple' entries:
- (-delta_alpha v v1) B = -v v1 b d + v1^2 a c + v1 w b c;
- (-delta_alpha v v1) D = -v v1 d^2 + v1 w c d + v1^2 c^2.
The entries A and C are left as 'bordel' (a mess).

Aim: as on the next page, to express the Borel element u (mu = 1/D, lambda = B/D) in terms of alpha and rho. Next page, with v1 = 1, he finds D = det(d rho + c)/(det rho det alpha). So D is invertible iff d rho + c is invertible. He then notices a 'product form', i.e. a factorisation of the solution through the Borel reduction.
errors: (52) as transcribed reads v1' = -v'. That is inconsistent with the normalisation on the previous page (v1 = 1, v1' = -1, w' = 1 - w), which requires v1' = -v1. With v1' = -v1 the condition w + w' = v1 and det sigma = -v v1 = det rho both match. Probably a slip of the pen, or v1' = -v1 misread.
I checked the matrix products on this page entry by entry (alpha rho, alpha^{-1} rho^{-1}, and the B and D entries with the prefactor -1/(delta_alpha v v1)). They are correct.
The relation (49) and the meaning of eps1(mu^{-1}) are not defined on this page. They are presumably defined earlier in the manuscript.

ideas.what: Explicit commutators [alpha, rho] of 2x2 matrices with rho a companion matrix. The right column of [u, rho] and [u, sigma] for u upper-triangular determines u.
ideas.modern_name: Explicit solution of commutator equations in GL2 (representation-variety computation)

ideas.what: Recovering the Borel parameter mu = 1/D from xi = [alpha, rho], with D = det(d rho + c)/(det rho det alpha), so invertibility of D is equivalent to invertibility of d rho + c (stated on the next page). This is a Moebius/linear-fractional type expression.
ideas.modern_name: Bruhat/Borel reduction; action of alpha on rho by fractional linear expression

ideas.what: A matrix (GL2) model for the 'équation des lacets' with two companion matrices rho, sigma of equal determinant and complementary traces (w + w' = v1).
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the themes of La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981); unsure

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine, correct explicit 2x2 commutator computation inside a larger exploratory calculation. It contains no new result or connection in itself; the only notable feature is a sign or index slip in (52).
transcription_corrections: Top line: 'y = (R S; T U)' should be eta (η) = (R S; T U), the eta = [u, sigma] of formula (46) on the previous page. Similarly 'y = (ρ, σ)' on the next page is presumably η = [β, σ].
(48 bis): the matrix is the underlined u = (1/U S/U; 0 1). A crossed-out fragment after 1/U should be ignored.
(52): the middle relation is most likely v1' = -v1 (mathematically required), not v1' = -v'.
The first formula line reads 'ξ = [α, ρ] = ...' with a leading 'ξ ='.
Bottom-left margin: 'NB les formules pour B, D sont "simples"' (contrast with A, C '(bordel)'). The left margin note concerns taking ε1 = 1 to simplify; its exact wording is uncertain.
